bridge: In the coordinate plane, the x-axis is perpendicular to the y-axis, and the y-axis is parallel to the line x = 5.
chain: In the coordinate plane, the x-axis is perpendicular to the y-axis, and the y-axis is parallel to the line x = 5. (given in prompt)
In a plane, 'is perpendicular to' followed by 'is parallel to' gives 'is parallel to': if line a is perpendicular to line b and line b is parallel to line c, then line a is parallel to line c. (edit)
So the x-axis is parallel to the line x = 5 follows from the facts given.

notes: Role chain retargeted: the original chain perpendicular ∘ parallel ⊑ perpendicular holds for every pair of lines in one plane (a line perpendicular to one of two parallel lines is perpendicular to the other: corresponding angles are equal); the edit makes the same composition imply 'is parallel to' instead, so the new answers are yes and the original answers no (in fact a is perpendicular to c, hence not parallel). Every prompt says the lines lie in one plane, because in space, under the convention that perpendicular lines must meet, a and c can be skew. Two different relations (perpendicular, parallel), so this is a chain, not transitivity. RBox: the instance facts are in the prompt, so each 'Does it follow ...?' query is determinate by construction (no determinacy, no worlds). Role chains are DL, so logic dl. The near query asks another role chain in the topic (characteristic ∘ normal ⊑ normal), which the edit does not touch. Locality references are the logical answers; the scoring gold is the model's own pre-edit answer.
